name: הוצאת גורם משותף – abc − bcd עם מקדמים (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if q=0 then abs(p) else igcd2(q,mod(p,q))

questiontext:
Factorise the following:

\[ {{CT:0}}. \]

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: The common factor is the highest common factor (hcf) of the coefficients times every letter that appears in all the terms, each with its lowest power. Divide every term by it, write the quotients in a bracket, and check by expanding.
Step 1 — The common factor
The terms are \({{CT:1}}\) and \({{CT:2}}\). The hcf of the coefficients \({{CT:3}}\) and \({{CT:4}}\) is \({{CT:5}}\), since

\[ {{CT:3}}={{CT:5}}\cdot {{CT:6}},\qquad {{CT:4}}={{CT:5}}\cdot {{CT:7}} \]

and the numbers \({{CT:6}}\) and \({{CT:7}}\) have no common factor other than \(1\). The letters \(b\) and \(c\) appear in both terms (each to the power \(1\)); \(a\) and \(d\) each appear in one term only. So the common factor is

\[ {{CT:8}} \]

Step 2 — Dividing each term by the common factor
Each term divided by \({{CT:8}}\):

\[ \frac{{{CT:1}}}{{{CT:8}}}={{CT:9}},\qquad \frac{{{CT:2}}}{{{CT:8}}}={{CT:10}} \]

The quotients go into the bracket:

\[ {{CT:0}}={{CT:8}}\left({{CT:11}}\right) \]

Step 3 — Check and answer
Check by expanding the brackets:

\[ {{CT:8}}\cdot {{CT:9}}-{{CT:8}}\cdot {{CT:12}}={{CT:0}} \]

(Taking out \({{CT:13}}\) instead gives the equivalent form below.) So the factorised form is

\[ {{CT:0}}={{CT:14}}. \]
